ideas: Skills games can develop, like strategy and teamwork
Games as a way to relax and socialise
When playing too much becomes a problem

phrases.meaning: forget how much time has passed
something useless to spend time on

model: I don't think video games are a waste of time, as long as people play them in moderation. First, many games arguably develop useful skills. Strategy games improve problem-solving skills, and online team games teach you to work as a team and think on your feet. For example, my younger brother plays a football management game, and he's learned quite a lot about budgeting and planning from it, to be honest. Another reason is that games can be a great way to relax and socialise. I tend to play for about an hour to unwind after work, and it's also how I stay in touch with my university friends, who now live in different cities. We meet online every Friday night and chat while we play. Of course, it's easy to lose track of time, and some people do become addicted, which can affect their studies or sleep. So I'd say limits are important. But overall, games seem to me to be just another hobby, and they can be really valuable if they're balanced with other activities.
